kevin: Quick heads-up — saw a perf regression in canary when multi-variant routing hits continuous batching.
anya: context? which service / metric?
kevin: svc=chat-infer, canary pool C. perfbot alerted: 95p token latency +12% vs baseline over last 10m.
perfbot: ALERT svc=chat-infer pool=canary metric=token_latency_95p change=+12% window=10m
lee: any recent deploys to the runtime kernels or compat mapping?
matt: rolled the new kernel-selector last night (better int8 kernels). I added permissive compat for a couple of variants to reduce failures.
kevin: think it’s interplay between permissive compat sets and batching. When compat expands, batcher mixes variants -> larger frag/slice mixing -> kernel fallback to slow path and KV cache thrash.
sara: can you paste a short config / snippet of batcher settings we replicated in canary?
kevin: sure:

```
batcher {
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_wait_ms: 8
  token_budget_target: 0.72
  queue_policy: per-queue-hetero
  compat_set_mode: permissive
}
```

anya: token_budget_target 0.72 is aggressive for mixed-variant traffic. with compat_set_mode=permissive we likely get high fragmentation -> smaller effective homogenous batches -> more kernel switches.
lee: also seeing KV cache evictions in the logs around the same timestamps — likely fragmentation increases unique cache keys.
kevin: exact log excerpt:

```
[2026-03-16T15:21:12.342Z] pool=canary shard=3 batch_id=4428 variants=[v1,v2,v3] kernel=fallback_slow kv_evictions=23 batch_tokens=312
[2026-03-16T15:21:12.350Z] pool=canary shard=3 batch_id=4429 variants=[v2] kernel=fast_int8 kv_hits=92 batch_tokens=480
```

matt: interesting — mixed batches causing fallback_slow. maybe our kernel-selector preference picks a fallback kernel when not all variants share the same kernel/quantization.
sara: quick probe we can run:
- force compat_set_mode=strict in canary
- reduce max_batch_wait_ms from 8 -> 4
- lower token_budget_target 0.72 -> 0.62

anya: +1 for incremental. strict compat will reduce fragmentation but may increase queue wait and decrease throughput.
kevin: wanted to check trade-off curve. can we run a two-run experiment: strict vs permissive with same other params, capture 50k requests each, profile KV eviction, kernel-switch %, and 95p latency.
dev-bot: experiment created: exp/flow-batch-compat-210246 — runs in canary, owners: @kevin @anya
lee: I'll add perf traces and kv metrics to the experiment dashboard.
matt: also add kernel-selector debug logging for those batches (compact mode) — need to see why fallback chosen.
anya: note: if we tighten token_budget_target it will bias batch formation to prefer homogeneity (it avoids accepting large hetero batches).
sara: TL;DR hypothesis: permissive compat + high token_budget -> aggressive coalescing across variants -> kernel fallback + KV thrash -> 95p latency regression.
kevin: agreed. next steps:
- (kevin) flip compat_set_mode=strict for 2h A/B test (start in 10m)
- (anya) run the token_budget sweep 0.62/0.68/0.72 under both compat modes
- (lee) capture kv_evictions, kernel_switch_rate, batch_size_hist, p95 latency
- (matt) keep kernel-selector verbose logs for the test window

matt: FYI if strict causes too many single-variant small batches we can try per-queue affinity heuristics first (prefer same-variant coalescing before cross-variant fill).
anya: also consider lowering max_batch_tokens to reduce cross-variant mixing at the tail.
kevin: ok launching now. will report back with first 30m snapshot.
perfbot: RUN_STARTED exp=exp/flow-batch-compat-210246 owners=[kevin,anya] time=2026-03-16T15:35:00Z
sara: thanks — watching the dashboard.
kevin: first 30m: strict mode p95 down ~8%, kv_evictions -60%, kernel_fallback_rate -84%. throughput down ~3%.
anya: that’s promising — small throughput hit but big latency and cache improvement. seems like the regression source.
lee: log sample shows fewer mixed-variant batches and more consistent kernels.
matt: proposal: make strict compat the default for canary routing for now and we can invest on better cross-variant kernel alignment later.
kevin: agreed. I'll promote strict to canary default and open a follow-up to test affinity heuristics + kernel alignment.
dev-bot: change applied: compat_set_mode=strict pool=canary by kevin at 2026-03-16T16:10:14Z
anya: follow-up items: document perf numbers, plan experiments for per-queue affinity, evaluate cost impact (throughput -> cost) and update rollout playbook.
kevin: assigning follow-up tasks in JIRA.
matt: good work catching the interaction. small config tweaks beat bigger kernel rollbacks.
kevin: thanks all — will post full perf dump in the eng-runtime doc channel once I scrub logs.
anya: :thumbsup:
